title: The Power of Open-Hardware Solutions for Improving Transmission Electron Microscopy Experiments
content: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) is an indispensable tool for materials characterization, enabling direct observation of micro- and nano-scale structures with exceptional spatial resolution. However, despite its critical importance, the ability of research facilities to adapt TEMs to new experimental requirements is often constrained by the high cost and low availability of specialized equipment. Both funding and lead-time challenges can hinder the efficiency of workflows and limit the potential of TEM for scientific discovery. This presentation explores how "DIY" solutions can bridge this gap, offering accessible, customizable, and cost-effective alternatives to enhance and expand the utility of TEMs in the characterization workflow. By presenting three examples of varying complexity, we aim to not only demonstrate the immediate effectiveness of these tools but also to encourage a community-wide shift toward shared innovation and open-source solutions in electron microscopy.
